Had Covid19 not constrained access to the equipment, some of these concepts would have been tried out on the equipment. However, there is strong interest and commitment to investigate some of these concepts: Resonant mixing of rCF to homogenize them in thermoplastic fiber matrix The resonance acoustic mixing (RAM) technology generates acoustic waves via the resonant vibration of a simple, mechanically driven agitator. The agitator system is kept on a resonant frequency by a closely controlled electromechanical oscillator, generating intense circular-mixing zones, each with a diameter in the range of 50-60 micron, see Figure 82. In contrast to the bulk fluid flow induced by impeller mixing, which tends to localize mixing around regions near the impeller(s), the acoustic stream generates small eddies that are evenly dispersed throughout the process fluid. The created vortices homogenize process fluids faster while reducing energy consumption and heat generation, says the firm. RAM induces microscale turbulence through the propagation of acoustic waves, Figure 83. RAM reduces complexity of mechanical mixing: 60 unwanted heat generation, due to excessive hydrodynamic shear stresses; long and inefficient mixing times. RAM differs from ultrasonic methods in that its high-intensity sound energy occurs at a low (50- 60 Hz) frequency and is amenable to scaleup. Among RAM's ancillary benefits is the potential for previously prohibitive high-viscosity mixing. In one trial, a solid mixture of micron-sized powders was easily mixed with a viscous polymer resin at an 80 wt% solids loading in approximately 2 min. Exhibiting a viscosity in excess of 80 cP (centipoise), the material had been very difficult to mix with prior methods. Additionally, as RAM is noninvasive, it is also safer and more hygienic, allowing both toxic materials and contaminant-sensitive products to be mixed in sealed containers without the risk of exposure. The potential energy is stored in the springs and the kinetic energy is provided by plates, or masses, that are connected to the springs and are translated into a vertical motion. Resonant acoustic mixing is comprised of multiple masses and multiple springs, known as a three-mass system, that are simultaneously moving during mixing. The concept is to add such a system in-line to the SMC line referred to as SMC V2 where rCF would be processed through the RAM to homogenize the rCF and feed through the SMC line.
